title: Row/column permutation — BROKEN under an unseen key
why: The cipher permutes row order and column order independently, which preserves the multiset of whole rows and columns under every key. That structure is key-independent, so an attacker that never saw this key still recovers the image.

title: Key-independent permutation — positive control
why: This cipher's transform is identical for every key, so there is nothing key-specific to learn. The attack should and does recover the plaintext exactly. It proves the instrument can detect a leak.

title: Keyed permutation + keyed diffusion — RESISTS
why: The same attacker, same training budget, against the baseline cipher. Its same-key ceiling is 1.000, so it demonstrably CAN invert this cipher when the key is fixed — it simply learns nothing that transfers to a new key.

title: AES-128-CTR — negative control
why: A cipher with no known structural weakness. The attack must fail completely; if it did not, the pipeline would be leaking plaintext somewhere.
